purpose: This record measures shared mesh storage and one-pass intersection searches in the pinned Rust boolean engine.

variants.base: Pinned Rust engine with the existing inlining patch.
variants.sharing: Shared immutable topology through batch evaluation and disjoint composition.
variants.combined: Shared mesh storage and one intersection search for both halves of an overlapping exact split.

method.probes: On a fixed back-top mesh, batch subtraction uses three nonoverlapping box cutters. Split uses one of the same box cutters. Each process warms once, measures four operations, and checks the final mesh's triangle count and bit-exact volume. The CPU and RSS samples also cover import, warmup and verification.
method.split_trace: Existing MANIFOLD_TIMING trace counts complete intersection searches for three split calls per process: warmup, one operation and output verification. Trace runs are outside the timing samples.
method.workload: All normal native producers run in the standard dependency order with two active producer slots. Three pairs alternate order. Precompiled binaries are timed using the same frozen external files; each backend's generated exports feed its own dependent producers.
method.caches: No whole-producer cache hits or enclosure stage reuse. Each variant has its own import cache across rounds. Immutable content-addressed scene assets are shared.
method.scope: Workload elapsed time includes producer execution, export, dependency staging and output hashing. It excludes compilation, publication, and the admission wait. CPU sums producer user and system time. RSS is the largest single producer process peak; it is not the aggregate memory of all running jobs.
method.host: The timing lease excludes other scheduled heavy runs within a pair. Ordinary desktop services keep running.

validation.command: tools/run -- cargo test --release --locked -j 2 --manifest-path tools/hsm/Cargo.toml -p hsm-manifold -p hsm-kernel -p hsm-geometry -p hsm-enclosure-solid --lib --tests
validation.assembly_payload_check: For the retained pairs, compare mesh arrays and all assembly metadata, resolving changed content-addressed objects. The only differences allowed here are build-directory prefixes, their derived byte lengths and checksums. Compare every NPZ entry, including triangle-to-face mapping and source records.
